R4E-bear-walk-0004.name: By Whitetail Creek
R4E-bear-walk-0004.pressureWhy: 2.3 km on foot from the nearest parking (estimate).
R4E-bear-walk-0004.parkWhat: pull off on A78 Whitetail Ck Rd (gravel road)

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2019 (7 years old), 280 m S: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
Burn from 2018 (fire N41525), right here: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
S facing slope, 18 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Whitetail Creek 40 m SE: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from Village of Radium Hot Springs, about 51 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate). Via Hwy 95, Horse Creek Rd S, Hwy 1 (Trans-Canada Hwy E), Hwy 1 (Trans-Canada Hwy).
Park: 50.97594, -116.154, pull off on A78 Whitetail Ck Rd (gravel road). Map links below.
Walk: 2.3 km NE, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 509 m, about 97 min at 3 km/h.

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 4-35, Region 4. No baiting in Region 4. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-01, closures 2026-10-16.
